payload.text: The typed tool tier is generated from the dispatch table, PARAMETER SCHEMAS INCLUDED -- derived from the table's authored `args` and `flags` rather than hand-kept anywhere, WITHOUT THIS ROW NAMING THE DERIVATION MECHANISM. **It read `schemars-derived` until 2026-08-31, when the build was measured to derive them from the TABLE on purpose and to say why in its own header** (`mcp.rs`: *a doc comment on a derived type is an unreviewed publication channel -- the author is writing a comment and the consumer is reading a contract*), which is D37's qualification applied to the tier. **A criterion that RESTATES a decision it does not own becomes a second home the moment that decision moves** -- this row is scoped to what it owns, that the schemas are DERIVED and never hand-maintained, and cites D37 for the mechanism. Amended by vc under the standing pen, on ic's finding, on the identical grounds and repair as `AC-00.3`'s transport clause. **Each entry DECLARES two fields the generator needs and the table does not carry today -- whether it is exposed on the MCP surface, and whether it READS or MUTATES -- and a row declaring neither is REFUSED.** (ic, EXP-03, raised 2026-08-15 before WP-09 opened, by reading this AC against the artefact it names.) Measured across all 103 rows: neither fact is present or derivable. `observed.side_effects` sits on 10 of 103, so **its absence means "not recorded", not "no side effects"** -- absence-as-meaning in the one place it decides whether an agent may close a steel thread. Without the fields a generator has exactly two options and both are defects: expose everything, so `intent mcp` becomes a tool that starts an MCP server from inside one; or carry a skip list, which is **a hand-maintained command list living one command away from AC-09.4, which forbids hand-maintained command lists** -- correct when typed and silently wrong at the next command added, because the act that invalidates it is not the act that updates it. **DECLARED per row, never derived from the verb**, and the proof that derivation fails is in the surface itself: `st sync` and `sync` are different commands sharing a spelling, and **`ac gate` reads while `wp done` consults the same gate and writes**. The refusal is what makes it hold -- with it there is no default to drift; **for a HUMAN resolving an uncertain row the safe directions are opposite** (`exposed` defaults toward no, `mutates` defaults toward yes), since a command wrongly omitted is an inconvenience and one wrongly included lets an agent run `daemon`, and a mutation mislabelled as a read lets an agent close a thread believing it is querying. **EXTENDED 2026-08-17 (vc, on ic's finding, under hv's standing grant): the generated tool DESCRIPTION -- not only the parameter schema -- carries `read_or_mutate` and, for a mutation, `recoverability`, in the D45 projection order the CLI guide already uses.** As written this AC obliged the generator to describe a tool's ARGUMENTS and obliged it to say nothing about what calling it does to the estate. **The consequence is already declared in the table and is not hypothetical: `at green`, `at red`, `at na` and `ext new` are all `exposed_on_mcp: true` AND `recoverability: one-way`** -- one-way because issue 0033 destroys the row's authored note, 1,447 characters measured on AT-03.12 and 14,253 at risk across 34 rows. **So the identical destructive operation would warn a CLI agent at the point of call and say nothing at all to an MCP agent**, which is the surface with less context. **D45 does not license the omission and reading it that way inverts it**: hv ruled the CLI precise and MCP imprecise, and `imprecise` is a claim about capability granularity, not about disclosure -- an agent with less context needs the safety fact more, not less. **This invents no policy and adds no field**: `recoverability`, its vocabulary, its refusal and its renderer all exist and are proven on the CLI surface, and this is one more projection of the same declaration, which is the whole argument for why `recoverability` is intrinsic to a row rather than an exposure flag. **Ruled BEFORE the tier is built deliberately** -- today it costs a sentence in an AC, and after WP-09 it is a change to what agents have already been told. **Sharpened by `design.md:310-320`, which is the same cut**: `schemars` lifts `///` into the JSON Schemas and a `///` on a derived type is _"an unreviewed publication channel -- the author is writing a comment and the consumer is reading a contract"_. **The generated description will carry prose either way; the only question this settles is whether that prose is the safety fact or whatever doc comment happens to sit on the type.**
